web.title: 30 African Startups That Raised Funding in 2026 (So Far)
web.description:
[Back to Blog](https://startupmaphub.com/blog)

African startups raised **$1.44 billion in the first half of 2026** — slightly ahead of the $1.42 billion raised in H1 2025, but across far fewer deals: just 146 disclosed rounds versus 252 a year earlier. Here are 30 companies that actually got funded this year, and what each deal tells you about where capital is flowing.

The numbers come from [TechCabal Insights](https://insights.techcabal.com/1-44-billion-raised-in-the-first-half-of-2026/), whose trackers put the half-year split at $749 million in Q1 and $692 million in Q2 — $818 million in equity, $614 million in debt and $9 million in grants. [Africa: The Big Deal](https://www.linkedin.com/company/africa-the-big-deal/), which counts only $100k+ deals, tracked $843 million across 160 deals from January to May, split almost evenly between equity and debt — a marked shift from 12–18 months ago, when equity's share sat above 70 percent.

One caveat before the list: not every raise is announced with a press release, and several strong deals this year were undisclosed. Amounts are as disclosed by the companies or tracked by TechCabal Insights, Africa: The Big Deal and our own database.

## All 30 at a glance
| Startup | Country | Sector | Round | 2026 amount |
|-|-|-|-|-|
| Stabyl | Nigeria | Fintech | Pre-seed | $2.7M |

## The growth rounds: debt does the heavy lifting
**GoCab** raised a **$45 million** hybrid round in February — equity from E3 Capital and JANNGO Capital plus significant debt — to scale ride-hailing in Francophone West Africa.

**MAX** raised **$32 million** in equity and asset-backed financing, starting with a $24 million January round, to finance vehicles for commercial drivers and push its fleet electric. **Zeno**, the battery-swap motorcycle maker operating in East Africa, raised **$25 million** in March.

$4M–$15M • Series A & big seeds

## The Series A club — and Morocco's quiet breakout
**WafR** raised a **$4 million seed** in January for retail-tech, and **Enakl** took **$2.3 million** to modernise shared commuting in Casablanca.

Under $3M • Seed & pre-seed

## The early-stage survivors: small cheques, sharp theses
Early-stage equity was the hardest money to raise in 2026 — which makes the companies that closed rounds worth studying.

In AI, Nairobi's **AethexAI** raised a **$3 million pre-seed** led by 4DX Ventures and Enza Capital to build customer-support and voice automation for African markets ( [our full breakdown](https://startupmaphub.com/blog/aethexai-raises-3-million-2026)).

**Zimi Charge** raised **$2.6 million** from the Development Bank of Southern Africa and Keyo Ventures for EV charging in South Africa. Cascador's catalytic funding awards backed three Nigerian companies in June: **Agriarche** ($1.8 million, agri supply chains), **Koolboks** ($1.5 million, solar-powered freezers) and **Powerstove** ($1.3 million, IoT-enabled clean cookstoves). **Breaze Delivery** raised **R20 million (~$1.23 million)** from Knife Capital and Kalon Venture Partners for township e-commerce logistics ( [our coverage](https://startupmaphub.com/blog/breaze-delivery-raises-2026)), and **Eja-Ice** secured **$1 million** from All On for off-grid solar cold-chain in Nigeria ( [deal notes](https://startupmaphub.com/blog/eja-ice-raises-1-million-2026)).

## What these 30 deals tell you about 2026
Half the money went to seven companies; meanwhile 26 startups raised above $100k in January — the lowest tally since at least 2020. If you're raising a $5–15 million round right now, you're in the most competitive segment of the market.

web.description:
[![Logistics Attracts $780 Million, Overtaking Fintech in African Startup Funding](https://www.wearetech.africa/media/k2/items/cache/20347e1f34163762552f3899b577f4fd_L.jpg)](https://www.wearetech.africa/media/k2/items/cache/20347e1f34163762552f3899b577f4fd_XL.jpg)

# Logistics Attracts $780 Million, Overtaking Fintech in African Startup Funding
By : Samira Njoya

- **African logistics and transport startups raised $780 million between January and September 2026, ahead of fintech, which attracted $760 million.**
- **Spiro and Moove secured a combined $595 million, accounting for about 76% of the funding raised by the logistics and transport sector during the period.**
- **African startups raised $2.16 billion in the first nine months of 2026, down about 4% from $2.24 billion a year earlier, while Nigeria led country rankings with $635 million.**

African logistics and transport startups raised $780 million between January and September 2026, surpassing fintech's $760 million, according to data published on Tuesday, October 20, by Africa: The Big Deal. The two sectors accounted for 36% and 35%, respectively, of the total funding recorded during the period.

Electric motorcycle company Spiro raised $345 million, while Moove, which finances vehicles for drivers working with mobility platforms, secured $250 million.

Together, the two companies raised $595 million, representing about 76% of the funding attributed to logistics and transport during the first nine months of the year. Their transactions therefore accounted for most of the sector's fundraising activity.

At least 80 fintech companies each raised $100,000 or more between January and September 2026, according to Africa: The Big Deal. This figure exceeded the number of funded companies in any other sector.

African startups raised $2.16 billion during the first nine months of 2026, compared with $2.24 billion over the same period in 2025, representing a decrease of about 4%.

Nigeria attracted $635 million in startup funding between January and September 2026, placing it ahead of Egypt, which secured $445 million.

Nigeria's total more than doubled from the $247 million recorded during the first nine months of 2025, according to data reported by Africa: The Big Deal. The country therefore strengthened its position as the continent's leading startup funding destination during the period.

**Samira Njoya**

Nigeria startup funding reached US$635 million in the first nine months of 2026, reclaiming Africa’s top position for the first time since 2022.

Nigerian startups raised US$635 million between January and September 2026. That compares with US$247 million in the same period of 2025 — a 157 per cent increase, according to funding data published in October 2026. The result returned Nigeria to the continent’s startup-funding lead.

It is also the highest recorded January-to-September total for Nigeria since 2022. By FurtherAfrica’s reading of the numbers, the rebound reflects a small group of large transactions. That distinction matters for investors assessing whether the momentum is repeatable.

## **Large rounds drive the rebound**
[Moove](https://www.moove.io/) led the charge. Moove provides financial services to drivers and transport operators across Africa.

Together, these four deals account for the bulk of Nigeria’s nine-month total.

Top Nigerian startup funding rounds Jan–Sep 2026

Source: October 2026 funding reports

Moove’s round alone represented approximately 68 per cent of Nigeria’s August 2026 funding. That single month generated around US$364 million — illustrating how quickly one large deal can reshape a country’s annual ranking.

Nigeria’s funding lead is real, but its concentration makes deal quality more important than headline volume.

## **What does the deal mix mean for investors?**
The sectoral tilt is clear. These segments attract large rounds when companies combine vehicle access, operating finance and payments infrastructure in a single platform.

The table below shows how Nigeria’s position compares with its two closest rivals, based on October 2026 country-level funding data.

Investors should watch whether funding broadens beyond the four leading transactions in the final quarter of 2026.
